The Big Story · Society

Japan lost 530,000 people. Its foreign population grew by 325,000.

The newest official estimate shows one country moving in two directions. Immigration is reshaping daily life, but the fall in children and rise in people over 75 reveal a harder arithmetic.

Demography · The age split

Children fell 2.6%. People over 75 rose 2.26%.

The latest final estimate counts 13.263 million children under 15, down 353,000 in a year. The population aged 75 or older added 476,000.

Japanese word of the day人口 · じんこう · jinkō

Population. 人 means “person” and 口 literally means “mouth,” but together they refer to the number of people living in a place.

You may also see 人口減少 (jinkō genshō), “population decline,” and 外国人人口 (gaikokujin jinkō), “foreign population.” Learn words in context with DraMap for iOS.
